title: Physiological Variables of EVA Participants--An Update
archive_status: Data preservation is complete. All datasets are publicly available.
notes: Downloaded: tabular files (xls/xlsx/csv/txt) and PDF reports up to 50 MB. Every Excel sheet is also saved as '<file>__<sheet>.csv' (raw cell grid, no header detection).
Not downloaded: figure images (tif/jpg) - they are rendered graphs; their URLs are listed under skipped_files.
Downloaded files are untrusted data: parse only, never open macros / execute.
LSAH newsletter tables: cohort aggregates by age group only (BMI, % body fat, VO2max, max heart rate). No per-person data, no time points relative to flight. Not importable to observation.

files.dataset_name: Age and Gender Distribution of Astronaut Groups at Time of Examination
files.dataset_description:
This graph depicts the age and gender distribution of Shuttle and EVA astronaut groups at the time of examination.

Reference: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Physical Activity for a Healthy Lifestyle. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. November 2000;9(2):1-2.

files.dataset_name: Select Physical Exam Parameters for non-EVA Shuttle Astronauts
files.dataset_description:
This graph depicts body mass index (BMI), percent body fat, VO2 max, and maximum heart rate for 174 Shuttle astronauts who did not perform extravehicular activities (EVAs).

Reference: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Physical Activity for a Healthy Lifestyle. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. November 2000;9(2):1-2.

files.dataset_name: Select Physical Exam Parameters for Shuttle Astronauts Performing EVA
files.dataset_description:
This graph depicts body mass index (BMI), percent body fat, VO2 max, and maximum heart rate for 51 Shuttle astronauts who performed extravehicular activities (EVAs).

Reference: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Physical Activity for a Healthy Lifestyle. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. November 2000;9(2):1-2.

skipped_files.dataset_description:
According to the Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health (LSAH) Lifestyle Questionnaire (LSQ), 72.3% of the responding 220 NASA astronauts and 38.2% of the responding 781 LSAH comparison participants list jogging/running among their various physical activities. Of the responding 32,440 National Health Interview Survey 1998 (NHIS) participants, 10.6% choose jogging/running among their various physical activities. In addition, 24.5%, 49.2%, and 43.2%, respectively, choose walking among their various physical activities.

Reference: National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Physical Activity for a Healthy Lifestyle. In: Longitudinal Study of Astronaut Health Newsletter. November 2000;9(2):1-2.
